structure.title: Between courts
structure.text: Shifts between Egypt and Rome give Antony's commitments competing settings, languages, and measures of success.

structure.title: Alliances under strain
structure.text: Political and intimate decisions become harder to separate as the relationship enters public conflict.

people.name: Antony
people.text: One of the three men who rule the Roman world, a great soldier who has let pleasure in Alexandria pull him away from his duties in Rome.

people.name: Cleopatra
people.text: The queen of Egypt, theatrical, quick-witted and changeable, who holds Antony with a mix of devotion and calculation that keeps everyone guessing.

people.name: Octavius Caesar
people.text: Julius Caesar's young heir and Antony's colleague in power: cool, patient and disciplined, everything Antony in Egypt is not.

context.title: Love between rulers
context.text: The lovers' decisions direct armies, households, and alliances. A private retreat is difficult when other people's security depends on them.

context.title: Competing descriptions
context.text: Roman and Egyptian observers describe the same conduct differently. Admiration and contempt help construct the lovers' public identities.
context.takeaway: Ask whose standard governs the description.

notice.why: Distance gives others power over what lovers know.
Grand language makes personal feeling compete with empire.

opening: Antony has responsibilities across the Roman world and an excellent reason to neglect them in Egypt. Cleopatra makes being with her feel grander than the business calling him away, but neither lover can stop being a ruler long enough to become merely private. Shakespeare gives their attraction the extravagance of people accustomed to changing other lives with a decision. Pleasure, jealousy, strategy, and performance become difficult to separate when the relationship everyone is gossiping about can also alter who governs an empire.
